Instead, I spent the day catching up with some great folks, so I'm going to embarass some of them now:

4. @bentossell the tall Welsh gentleman in pink - has an amazing newsletter in Ben's Bites

5. @thenanyu the man who brings taste and craft to everything he touches from Linear to OpenAI

6. @illscience my favorite a16z partner that I've met (because @joshelman still hasn't met me in person 😅)

7. @fishmanaf a great product leader but more importantly the most buff dad ever

8. @tomkrcha the founder behind @pendev one of my favorite AI design tools

9. @victornunez who still makes time to answer my dumb DMs at 11 pm despite working at OpenAI and having 3 kids
@nealmohan how about letting users (or at least parents) opt out of shorts entirely

Had a brief Q&A with @sama today. Here’s my quick paraphrase of his answers:

1. How are Dots different from other personal agents?

Plenty of agents will book restaurants for you. The ambition for Dots is bigger: Expand what you can do and earn enough trust to handle complex tasks. Dots are powered by Astra.

2. When will AI deliver a breakthrough in treating cancer and other diseases?

We could see something next year that helps treat one type of cancer, though the FDA timeline is difficult to predict.

3. One other answer that stuck with me:

He’s strongly against young kids scrolling through short-form videos. I feel the same way.

• Ballooning US debt and deficits
• AI bonds soaking up cash
• Inflation stuck above 2%
• Iran tensions keeping oil high

Texas produces a huge share of U.S. crude and refining capacity, and it still had to loosen road-diesel rules just to keep trucks moving.

Chainflip 挡了一刀，但 AML 追不上洗币速度：慢雾余弦复盘 Bitget 赃款新动向

慢雾 @SlowMist_Team 创始人余弦 @evilcos 今天发文说了一个挺扎心的事实。他跟踪 Bitget @bitget 被盗资金好几个小时，看到 Chainflip @Chainflip 确实在努力拦截朝鲜🇰🇵黑客洗币，但 AML/KYT 风控的速度就是追不上洗币的速度。

9 月 29 日凌晨，黑客地址先收到约 6262 枚 SOL，随后拆成 2000、2100、2162.5 枚三笔送进 Chainflip。前两笔顺利通过，第三笔被服务商拒收，退回到另一个黑客地址。大约 10 分钟后，这笔约 2162 枚 SOL 经过一个新的中转地址，再次送进 Chainflip，这次过了。

余弦总结的黑客套路是：用自动化脚本把钱大量打散，通过各种跨链桥分流；被拦下就立刻换路径重试，最后统一换成 BTC，再用 CoinJoin 混币。用他的话说，这是一个「不断在演变的洗币工程」。

推荐阅读《播客笔记｜Michael Saylor：留给我们的 BTC “淘金热”只剩 9 年，2035 年后大门将彻底关上》

https://t.co/nciBtKhx6f

.@saylor 在 @binance 的最新访谈中，给出了他对比特币定价逻辑和时间边界的完整推演，他认为比特币的投资机会窗已不足 10 年。

抛开他持仓 84 万枚 $BTC 的立场，视频中这 4 个基于数学和宏观环境的判断值得参考：

1. 明确的时间边界：从现在到 2035 年是最后的红利期。2035 年，99% 的比特币将被挖出。此后，BTC 的增长曲线将逐渐平缓，大约 20 年后，其年化收益将降至仅比标普 500 高 3-5 个点，超额收益期结束。

2. 下一个价格引擎：比特币货币化分为 ETF、财库储备、数字信贷和银行放贷四步。前三步已经发生，未来 36 个月的核心驱动力将是“银行放贷”——逻辑类似房地产，当银行开始接受 BTC 抵押放贷，资产价格才会被真正撬动。

3. 真实通胀的折算：普通人关注 3% 的 CPI（工业品通胀），而资金关注 15% 的“资本成本”通胀（稀缺资产的涨幅）。

AI 会让服务变便宜，但凭空变不出市中心的绝版地段和毕加索的真迹。在生产力越丰裕的时代，绝对稀缺的资产越贵。

4. 黄金的数学劣势：黄金每年约有 2% 的新增供给，这意味着储存在黄金里的购买力每 36 年会被稀释一半，而比特币的通胀最终趋零。

看懂这套逻辑，就能理解他当前发股、发债买币的底层框架。具体论述见视频👇

tweets.text:
See also @jgebbia's talk below:
https://t.co/oYrnxqAPcw

Impressive. This set of talks, along with the new America dot gov website, has the unmistakable feel of an Apple launch event. They're rebooting the federal government as a tech startup. Several observations.

(1) First, with this new AI interface to the entire federal government, if it works as promised, there won't be a single American who can't say their life wasn't helped at least in part by AI, or that the benefits accrued solely to zillionaires. This in itself cannily mitigates anti-datacenter sentiment.

(2) Second, Joe Gebbia and Marco Rubio's talks on simplifying name changes and passport filings introduce a completely new era where the US government is actually launching tangible features that benefit users.

(3) Third, this launch event in and of itself may visibly drive reform. It could become much more important than the State of the Union. Unlike laws, code is user-visible, and can be instantly audited by the public, as Obama found out with the failed obamacare website launch. So: the annual America dot gov event may be substance, whereas SOTU is traditionally optics. I wouldn't be surprised to see the President present at the next one.

(4) Fourth, this kind of event is a perfect example of where tech and red cooperate best. They both hate bureaucracy. Automating paperwork with code reduces the power of statists over both capitalists and nationalists. It's also hard to undo by other admins: once you digitize a process, hard to turn it back to paper.

(5) Fifth, it's an obvious point perhaps, but think about how much influence YCombinator has had in 20 years. From Gebbia's Airbnb joining their 2009 batch to a complete overhaul of the user interface of the US bureaucracy, and thus the US government.

(6) Sixth, this is another take on the network state. The functional part of the US (the network, meaning tech) is merging with and partially reforming the dysfunctional part (the state, meaning bureaucracy) by automating 20th century paper forms.

As a tech startup, there will no doubt be bugs and user issues and so on, but unlike with paper laws those issues will be visible and the code fixes will be verifiable. A new era of AI America. Rooting for them.
